samples.sample_label: Matched UK cross-listed vs UK-only firms (audit fee litigation risk test)
samples.sample_unit_detail: 275 US cross-listed and 275 UK-only matched controls
samples.period_detail: Matched sample drawn from 1996 pooled frame (3,666 firm-years across years in frame).

sample_unit.quote: We first run our analyses on a sample obtained by matching cross-listed observations with observations listed only in the UK.

sample_period.quote: sample frame consists of 3666 observations. This is comprised of 1299 firms in 1996,

data_sources.quote: obtained from the Financial Times Extel Company Analysis database.

missing_fields.sample_size: Matched N=550 implied by 275+275; paper does not state 550 explicitly.

data_section_full_text:
We first run our analyses on a sample obtained by matching cross-listed
observations with observations listed only in the UK. For every industry (SIC onedigit group) and size (LNTA) decile and within each year, cross-listed firms
(including both firms cross-listed in the US and those listed in some other foreign
country), are matched with an equal number of systematically selected (SEDOL
order) UK-only listed firms. For each industry-year-size group of cross-listed firms,
if there are not enough non-cross-listed firms available for the matching, then a
number of systematically selected (SEDOL order) cross-listed firms are dropped in
order to give equal numbers of cross-listed and non-cross-listed firms. This leads to a
sample containing 275 cross-listed (experimental) and 275 non-cross-listed (control)
